title: Learning Paradigms
description: Quick check on supervised, unsupervised, semi-supervised, transductive vs inductive, and Pavlovian conditioning.

questions.prompt: What are the applications of Supervised Learning given in the lectures/notes?
What are the applications of Unsupervised Learning given in the lectures/notes?
Semi-Supervised Learning exists because labelling all data is often impractical. Give the two main reasons why data isn't always labelled.
Match each Semi-Supervised Learning assumption to its description.
right: Data points in the same cluster are likely to have the same label
Close-together data points are likely to have the same label

questions.prompt: Match each learning approach to its description.
right: Makes predictions for a specific fixed set of unlabelled data, without necessarily learning a general rule
Learns a general rule from labelled data that can be applied to any new unlabelled data

questions.prompt: Arrange the stages of Pavlovian Conditioning in the correct order.
items: Before conditioning: food alone triggers salivation
Before conditioning: bell alone triggers no response
During conditioning: food and bell paired, reinforcing the association
After conditioning: bell alone triggers salivation
